caption: Newanforbi v. Shannon Smith, LCSW, CEO, et al.
claims: 42 U.S.C. §1983 (Monell + Individual Capacity); Bane Act (Cal. Civ. Code §52.1); Fraud / Negligent Misrepresentation; RICO (18 U.S.C. §1962(c)-(d))
status: Case Filed July 20, 2026 — Hon. Lisa J. Cisneros. Order filed July 23, 2026 required: (1) correct district IFP form by Aug. 13, 2026 — MOOTED July 24, 2026 by Plaintiff's direct payment of the $405 federal civil filing fee (Pay.gov, Case No. DCAN326CV007504); (2) the state court's demurrer decision by Aug. 13, 2026 for preclusion analysis — SATISFIED July 27, 2026, 17 days early, via Notice of Payment of Filing Fee and Filing of State Court Decision (Exs. A-C: signed Order, Tentative Ruling, and Minute Order from Matter 5). Motion for Protective Order DENIED WITHOUT PREJUDICE. Initial Case Management Conference set Oct. 22, 2026
defendants: HOPE Psychotherapy, Inc. (d/b/a HOPE Program), CASOMB-certified LCSW Professional Corporation (principal office: 1245 B Street, Hayward, CA 94541; 16 statewide locations); Shannon Smith, LCSW (CEO and Founder, individually)
key_facts: HOPE Psychotherapy, Inc. (d/b/a HOPE Program) is a CASOMB-certified, state-contracted sex offender management program (SOMP) operating under a CDCR vendor agreement that makes it a state actor for constitutional purposes under West v. Atkins, 487 U.S. 42 (1988). Shannon Smith, LCSW, is HOPE's CEO and founder, personally directing clinical and compliance policies across 16 California locations. The complaint alleges: (1) HOPE maintained a blanket institutional policy requiring all parolees to complete the full parole term before graduating from treatment, regardless of individual clinical progress — a practice judicially condemned in In re Dwyer (SC-080355A, San Mateo County Super. Ct., Mar. 20, 2023); (2) Shannon Smith directed retaliatory reporting to Plaintiff's parole agent, including logging no-shows for sessions Plaintiff attended (corroborated by HOPE_000142 and HOPE_000194 from Matter 5 discovery — a no-show logged despite an agent-confirmed technical error) and generating adverse CDCR Form 3043 treatment status reports; (3) HOPE billed CDCR at group ($100/session), CTM ($100/session), individual ($200/session), quarterly plan ($125), polygraph ($500), and psychological evaluation ($1,800) rates — generating approximately $106,000–$111,000 per parolee over a ten-year supervision term — while providing substandard treatment and retaliating against clients who exercised constitutional rights; (4) the foregoing conduct constitutes a RICO enterprise (18 U.S.C. §1962(c)-(d)) through a pattern of racketeering involving fraudulent billing to CDCR and false official reporting to parole agents. Prior W-2 records document CDL career earnings of $109,408+ over 2022–2024 (United Road, Keurig Dr Pepper, Tiger Lines LLC, US-1 Shorthaul, Lazer Spot Inc., Centerline Drivers); but-for earning capacity ~$72,000/year as a Class A CDL commercial driver. Philadelphia Indemnity Policy No. 067968 ($1M per-incident / $5M aggregate) provides insurance coverage. Discovery from the dismissed state case (Newanforbi v. Palacios et al., STK-CV-UF-2026-0001032, disposed July 15, 2026 on demurrer) produced 542 pages (Bates HOPE_000001–542) including HOPE's Clinical Operational Manual, Maintenance Curriculum, Employee Handbook, Preparatory Treatment Manual, Clinical Director job description, Plaintiff's homework records and internal completion audit, collateral notes, emails, and insurance policies. RFA No. 4 and No. 18 (HOPE), Nos. 6 and 8 (Palacios), and SROG Nos. 11 and 14 yielded admissions directly supporting Monell and RICO theories. Motion for Protective Order filed contemporaneously with the complaint seeks NDCA authorization to retain and use this discovery under equivalent protective-order terms, avoiding duplicative re-production.
procedural_status: Complaint (v2) docketed July 21, 2026 (Case Filed July 20, 2026), USDC N.D. Cal., Case No. 3:26-cv-07504, assigned to Hon. Lisa J. Cisneros. Federal successor to Newanforbi v. Palacios et al. (STK-CV-UF-2026-0001032), which was dismissed July 15, 2026 (demurrer sustained without leave to amend on exhaustion grounds). Docket: (1) Complaint filed, In Forma Pauperis pending; (2) Motion for Leave to Proceed In Forma Pauperis filed; (3) Proposed Summons filed; (4) Initial Case Management Scheduling Order with ADR Deadlines issued — Case Management Statement due 10/15/2026, Initial Case Management Conference set 10/22/2026, 1:30 PM, San Francisco (videoconference only); (5) Consent/Declination to Proceed Before a US Magistrate Judge filed; (6) Motion for Protective Order filed with supporting Declaration — seeks authorization to retain and use the 542 pages of HOPE discovery produced under the state Stipulated Protective Order (entered June 17, 2026), now that the state action is disposed; responses due 8/3/2026, replies due 8/10/2026. The state SPO restricted use to (1) the state action and (2) Newanforbi v. Derrick (E.D. Cal. 2:26-cv-00004-DJC-JDP); Plaintiff moves NDCA to extend equivalent protections to this federal action, avoiding duplicative re-production of the same documents. Case Management Conference packet mailed by the court July 21, 2026. July 23, 2026: Mag. Cisneros issued an Order (Doc 7) addressing three matters. (1) IFP: Plaintiff used a generic AO form rather than this district's specific form, and his answers (all 'No'/'N/A'/'None' except a $105.45 bank balance) lack context for the Court to assess credibility; Clerk directed to attach the district's own IFP form, which Plaintiff must complete and file by August 13, 2026 (with a separate statement explaining how he meets basic needs if it shows no income/expenses). (2) State court decision: Plaintiff ORDERED to file a copy of the state court's demurrer decision by August 13, 2026 so the Court can assess claim/issue preclusion. (3) Motion for Protective Order (Doc 6): DENIED WITHOUT PREJUDICE — the Court found it not obvious it has authority to alter the state court's document return-or-destroy deadline, and took judicial notice that Matter 3's MTD was still under submission (not yet resolved) at the time, so the state SPO's 'whichever is later' clock had not started running; denial preserves Plaintiff's ability to seek relief from the state court directly or renew the motion here once Defendants are served and appear. Note: the premise that Matter 3's MTD remained unresolved was overtaken the very next day — Mag. Peterson ruled on it July 24, 2026 (see Matter 3), which may now start that clock running. July 24, 2026: Plaintiff paid the $405.00 federal civil filing fee in full via Pay.gov (PayPal Transaction ID 64284393V9888364P, Agency Tracking ID 77460057867, Case No. DCAN326CV007504), mooting the IFP application and the district-form deadline the July 23 order otherwise set for August 13, 2026. The Pay.gov confirmation was forwarded to CAND Finance and entered on the docket the same day as Document 8. Dated July 27, 2026 and docketed July 30, 2026 as Document 9, Plaintiff filed a Notice of Payment of Filing Fee and Filing of State Court Decision (Re: Dkt. No. 7), satisfying both remaining items from the July 23 order 14 days ahead of the August 13 deadline. Section A requests the Court deem the IFP application (Dkt. No. 2) withdrawn given the fee payment and process the case as a paid filing. Section B attaches, as Exhibits A-C, the signed Order Sustaining Demurrer to FAC Without Leave to Amend (Jul. 15, 2026), the Tentative Ruling (dated Jul. 10, 2026), and the Minute Order (Jul. 15, 2026) from Matter 5 (Newanforbi v. Palacios et al., STK-CV-UF-2026-0001032), and clarifies for the Court's preclusion analysis that: (1) the signed order's stated ground ('fails to allege facts sufficient to state any cause of action') is broader than the court's actual reasoning in the Tentative Ruling and Minute Order, both of which rest specifically on failure to exhaust administrative remedies as a jurisdictional prerequisite — the court did not reach the merits of any of the seven state causes of action; (2) Shannon Smith was not a party to the state action (only Katie Palacios and HOPE Psychotherapy, Inc. were defendants there); and (3) no final judgment of dismissal has been entered in the state action as of July 27, 2026 — confirming, independently of Peterson's July 24 ruling in Matter 3, that the state Stipulated Protective Order's return-or-destroy clock (tied to a final judgment's appeal-period expiration) has not started running on the Matter 5 side either. Certificate of Service notes no Defendant has yet been served in this action, so no service on opposing parties was required for this filing. CORRECTION: the Document 9 Certificate of Service as filed incorrectly recited that the Notice was filed with the Clerk via the CM/ECF system; because Plaintiff has no CM/ECF filing credentials as a pro se litigant, the Notice was in fact mailed to the Clerk via USPS. Plaintiff prepared an Amended Certificate of Service correcting this, executed July 31, 2026 at Milpitas, California, for filing with the Court. UNRESOLVED DISCLOSURE GAP (flagged, not yet cured): this matter's preclusion analysis carefully discloses Matter 5 (Palacios/HOPE, state) to the court but nowhere mentions Matter 6 (Newanforbi v. HOPE et al., 2:26-cv-00195-TLN-AC) — an earlier federal action against the same HOPE entity on a closely related structural-conflict-of-interest theory (same ~$100k+/parolee CDCR billing rate, recomputed here over a longer horizon), voluntarily dismissed without prejudice May 21, 2026 with refiling expressly preserved. HOPE's own counsel (SLB) already put a federal judge on notice of a Matter 3/Matter 6 relationship via a Notice of Related Cases (ECF No. 5) in Matter 6 itself. This matter's Monell/RICO theory reads as substantially that refiling, but the connection to Matter 6 is not disclosed anywhere in this record or (so far as this file shows) to Judge Cisneros. A corrective disclosure should be considered alongside the Matter 20/24 gap noted in Matter 24.
damages: $249,000 – $1,510,000+: Lost CDL wages and career displacement (documented $109,408+ in 2022–2024 W-2s; $72K/yr but-for rate); §1983 compensatory and punitive damages (Shannon Smith individually); Bane Act §52.1 statutory damages ($25,000 per violation; multiple violations alleged); RICO treble damages (3× enterprise economic harm under 18 U.S.C. §1964(c)); attorney fees (42 U.S.C. §1988; RICO fee shifting).
risk: Favorable on state-actor theory — West v. Atkins controls for CDCR contractors. Monell requires proving a custom or policy: supported by blanket retention policy confirmed in In re Dwyer and HOPE's own Clinical Operational Manual (HOPE_000294 — verbatim 'Aftercare Phase' language tying treatment to full parole term). RICO adds substantial complexity and risk of dismissal (pattern and enterprise must be pleaded with particularity per Twombly); preserved as an aggressive-scenario multiplier. Insurance coverage through Philadelphia Indemnity ($1M per-incident / $5M aggregate) creates a realistic settlement floor. Shannon Smith's individual capacity exposure creates personal settlement pressure independent of HOPE's corporate coverage. 542 pages of discovery already in hand from the dismissed state case provides a substantial evidentiary head start unavailable in most §1983 cases at the filing stage.
